statements.impact_statement: RUSTSEC-2026-0173: the proc-macro-error2 crate, a helper for writing procedural macros, is no longer maintained, as its author confirmed. RustSec marks every proc-macro-error2 release as affected, reports no vulnerability in it and lists no patched version: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0173.html, https://github.com/GnomedDev/proc-macro-error-2/issues/17 . We downloaded every build-dev package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: 91 versions from 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only, and checked each download against the index checksum. 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times per architecture with different checksums; the copy the repository serves was the one read. No package contains a symbolic link. Each package holds one program, /usr/bin/build, a Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0, which contains no Rust code; a byte search of every ELF file in every build finds no zbus, zvariant or proc-macro-error name. No build of this package contains uv or any Rust crate, so the crate is not present.

We downloaded every build-fips-dev package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the authenticated DHI Alpine security repository, where the FIPS packages are published, for x86_64 and aarch64: 91 versions from 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only, and checked each download against the index checksum. 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times per architecture with different checksums; the copy the repository serves was the one read. RUSTSEC-2026-0173: the proc-macro-error2 crate, a helper for writing procedural macros, is no longer maintained, as its author confirmed. RustSec marks every proc-macro-error2 release as affected, reports no vulnerability in it and lists no patched version: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0173.html, https://github.com/GnomedDev/proc-macro-error-2/issues/17 . We downloaded every build-fips package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the authenticated DHI Alpine security repository, where the FIPS packages are published, for x86_64 and aarch64: 91 versions from 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only, and checked each download against the index checksum. 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times per architecture with different checksums; the copy the repository serves was the one read. No package contains a symbolic link. Every build carries the Go program /usr/bin/build, from 2.26.2-r1 also the Go program /opt/docker/dhi/yq and from 2.28.0-r1 also the Go program /usr/bin/dhi-source, all built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and containing no Rust code. From 2.27.1-r1 (2.27.1-r1 to 2.30.0-r0, 12 versions) each build also carries /opt/docker/dhi/uv, the uv 0.13.6 Rust program, of which these builds hold five different binaries per architecture. A byte search of every ELF file in every build finds zbus, zvariant and proc-macro-error names only in /opt/docker/dhi/uv. We read the crate list that cargo-auditable embeds in each uv binary (its .dep-v0 section) in every build on both architectures, and searched each distinct uv binary for strings. In every uv binary the crate list names proc-macro-error2 2.0.1, whose only user in that list is defmt-macros 1.1.0, a procedural-macro crate (proc-macro = true in its Cargo.toml) used by defmt, which the jiff date-time crates depend on. Procedural-macro crates and their dependencies are compiled for the Rust compiler and run inside it while uv is built; they are not linked into the uv program. No uv binary contains a proc-macro-error2 source path or the name proc_macro_error, while the same search finds source paths of other crates, such as zvariant-5.11.0/src/ and zbus-5.15.0/src/, in every one. The proc-macro-error2 code is not present in any build of this package.
